title.narrative: Industrial Waste Management and Cleanup Project

description.narrative: The Development Objective of the Project is to reduce contamination of Montenegro's natural resources and public health risks of exposure to this contamination from selected industrial waste disposal sites.

The Industrial Waste Management and Cleanup Project of Montenegro has an objective designed to reduce contamination of Montenegro?s natural resources and public health risks of exposure to this contamination from selected industrial waste disposal sites. The project consists of three components. The first component This component will finance the detailed design, construction, and supervision for the remediation of the Project Sites, including through the following measures: slope and dam stabilization; coverage; containment cells; in-site encapsulation; re-shaping; re-vegetation; drainage and other water management investments including groundwater management measures, if needed; and removal (including export) of hazardous and non-hazardous waste. Component two will support the Borrower and industries involved with management of the Project Sites in managing future industrial hazardous waste generation in a manner compliant with national and EU legislation, in strengthening the Borrower?s institutional and regulatory capacities in the field of industrial hazardous waste management, and in exploring options for developing infrastructure for industrial hazardous waste disposal at the national level. Finally, component three This component will support Project management and capacity building at EPA, including establishment of the PMU, and support for project monitoring and evaluation, including establishment of a monitoring and evaluation system, funding of audits, training, equipment, consultants? services, and incremental operating costs.

title.narrative: Number of industries related to the priority industrial waste disposal sites with arrangements for ongoing and future waste disposal in compliance with national legislation for solid waste management

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Target achieved</strong>. This indicator measures the number of industries that are related to the priority industrial waste disposal sites under the Project, with arrangements for ongoing waste disposal in compliance with national legislation for solid waste management. EPCG (power plant) has made arrangements for ongoing coal ash disposal in compliance with national legislation for solid waste management. </p>

title.narrative: Number of industries related to the priority industrial waste disposal sites with arrangements for ongoing and future waste disposal in compliance with national legislation for solid waste management

comment.narrative: Achieved and no more monitoring is needed.

title.narrative: Contaminated land managed or dump sites closed under the project

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Target achieved</strong>. This indicator measures the sum of the contaminated land managed and cleaned up at three sites (Gradac, Pljevla, and Bijela) under the Project. Because of changes in the project scope after the first restructuring, the target value has been reduced from 110 ha to 24 ha, As of December 1, 2022, the remediation was completed in two sites (Gradac and Pljevlja) and the cleanup at the Bijela site is also completed. Therefore, the (revised) target is fully achieved by the project closing. </p>

title.narrative: Contaminated land managed or dump sites closed under the project

comment.narrative: Remediation works completed on the two sites other than Bijela. The reported amount is based on the sum of the areas for the Gradac and Pljevlja sites (see intermediate indicators) and current completion of cleanup at the Bijela site (1.5 ha, now fully completed).

title.narrative: Reduction of pollution exposures paths by remediation measures

comment.narrative: Works at Gradac and Pljevlja being complete, and underway at the Bijela site have now resulted in managed pathways for migration of pollutants through water and air and now also through soil and groundwater, hence pathways have increased to 8. For around 53,00 tons of contaminated soil, temporary storage on site needs to be designed and installed. Although materials are at presents also stored on a safe manner, it is proposed to consider this target fully met (all 9 paths closed) when the temporary storage arrangement in Bijela are in place.

title.narrative: Reduction of pollution exposures paths by remediation measures

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Target achieved</strong>. The indicator was defined as the number of pollution exposure paths through (i) air, (ii) soil and groundwater, and (iii) run-off water, eliminated by remediation measures under the Project. Due to changes in the projectcope after the first restructuring, the target value was revised from 12 pollution exposure paths to 9 paths. By the Project closing, a total of nine (9) pollution paths are managed. with a temporary arrangement to securely store contamination soil in the Bijela site. </p>

title.narrative: Intermediate Result Indicator Two: Industrial dump site at Pljevlja closed under the Project

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Target achieved.</strong> This indicator measures the area of industrial dump site in Pljevlja (coal ash disposal site at the Maljevac landfill - Cassette II) closed under the Project. The original plan was to fully close and remediate the 53.5 ha ash disposal facility from the lignite-fired power plant in Pljevlja, owned and operated by EPCG.  However, developing a new ash disposal facility at the Sumane site during the project duration resulted in changes in the scope through restructuring. The revised approach to expand the existing site capacity and partial remediation (10 ha) of Cassett II. The remediation at the target coal ash disposal facility was completed in June 2021. The technical inspection to review the remediation was conducted in June 2022. The inspection confirmed that the remediation works had been completed in accordance with the design, building permit, technical norms, and standards, and the facility is ready to use.  The contractor has been carrying out necessary regular maintenance measures within the recultivated areas, including additional tree planting. EPCG will continue monitoring and maintenance in accordance with the design and national regulations, as this work is the result of the first phase of the remediation of the Maljevac landfill (with remaining Cassettes 1 and 3). </p>

title.narrative: Intermediate Result Indicator Two: Industrial dump site at Pljevlja closed under the Project

comment.narrative: Remediation works at the Pljevlja Maljevac site have started in the summer of 2019 and were fully completed and verified in 2022.

title.narrative: Intermediate Result Indicator One: Industrial dump site at Gradac closed under the Project

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Target achieved</strong>. This indicator measures the area of the industrial dumpsite at Gradac (mine tailing site) closed under the Project. The original tailing dumpsite(12.5 ha) was fully remediated as of June 2020. The technical inspection conducted in June 2022 to review the remediation work confirmed that i) the Gradac site was completely remediated in accordance with the design, building permit, technical norms and standards, and ii) the facility is ready to use. After the completion of the technical inspection, the contractor conducted the geodetic survey of the project site twice a year until October 2023. The measurements confirm that the reconstructed and recultivated landfill has been stable after the completion of remediation works.  </p>

title.narrative: Intermediate Result Indicator One: Industrial dump site at Gradac closed under the Project

comment.narrative: Remediation work has been completed at Gradac site.

title.narrative: Intermediate Result Indicator Three: Cleanup of Bijela site

comment.narrative:
To date 76,409 tons of waste materials have been exported including all the 68,463 tons of hazardous grit waste, the most challenging waste category. The main remaining challenge remains with the export of around 53,000 tons of contaminated soil. This causes 41% of waste still in need of export or utilization / disposal in Montenegro.
???????

title.narrative: Intermediate Result Indicator Three: Cleanup of Bijela site

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Target 75% acheived.</strong> This indicator measures the percentage of waste removed from the Bijela shipyard site, compared to the total identified removable industrial waste at the site from the beginning of the project. By project closing, a total of 98,783 tons of waste, including grit and contaminated soil, was removed from the Bijela shipyard site. However, about 33,000 tons of less contaminated soil remains and is securely stored through encapsulation at the project site. This soil is planned to stay in Bijela for three years and potentially could be used as the leveling layer on the solid waste disposal facility at the KAP location </p>

title.narrative: Intermediate Result Indicator Four: Design and works bidding documents completed for KAP sites

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Target achieved.</strong> The original indicator related to KAP site was 'Industrial dumpsite at KAP closed under the Project (Hectares)'. However, the loan amount for works at the KEP sites was canceled during the first restructuring. After the first restructuring, the original indicator was replaced by this new indicator to capture the results of the revised scope of the activities at the KAP sites (design, safeguards and bidding documents) financed by the Project. Design, safeguards, and bidding documents for (i) the red-mud basin and (ii) solid waste landfill at the KAP aluminum plant location were prepared, thus fully meeting the target.     </p>

title.narrative: Intermediate Result Indicator Five: Support further development of a national registration system for industrial and hazardous waste management

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Target achieved.</strong> A national registion system for industrial and hazardous waste management (called 3R) has been developed. A system has been integrated into the information system of the Ministry of Public Administration (availale at 3r-epa.gov.me)  with more than 80% of waste flows recorded. </p>

actual.value: System applied, 80% of waste flows recorded.
